# frimpomaasync.com

frimpomaasync.com builds practical business systems for owner-run service businesses. SynKasa handles the front desk. Siesie handles the repeating work behind it. Every build lives in the client's accounts and stays theirs.

There is a second audience with its own product. Soft Appeals recovers denied insurance claims for independent medical practices. It is the same idea pointed at healthcare: a hospital keeps a department for fighting denials and an independent practice does not, so Soft Appeals is that department, sized for the practice.

Primary slogan: "Watch it work before you pay."

Guarantee: "Live in 7 days, or you don't pay."

The guarantee covers the agreed system going live. It never promises a number of bookings, because bookings depend on the inquiries the business receives.

## Visitor path

1. Name the business leak on the homepage.
2. Take one same-day fix.
3. Watch the relevant working build.
4. Use the SynKasa fit form or Siesie application.
5. Book the confirmed 15-minute call.
6. Receive a recommendation.
7. Review the proposal and agreement.
8. Pay before onboarding begins.
9. Complete onboarding, build, testing, and approval.
10. Launch, train, and hand over.
11. Follow up on performance.
12. Request approved proof, a referral, care, or the next useful system.

The local leak finder, calculator, and Siesie check do not store or transmit visitor inputs.

## SynKasa

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/synkasa

Fit form: https://frimpomaasync.com/synkasa-fit

SynKasa is the flagship front desk, formerly sold as the Client Catcher. It answers calls, texts, and direct messages in the owner's voice, qualifies the inquiry, books the right time, and follows up.

Current tiers:

- Start: $555 once. Calls, texts, and direct messages are answered, qualified, and booked. Optional care is $99 a month.
- Grow: $1,500 once. Adds follow-up, reminders, review requests, quote chasing, and one dashboard. Optional care is $222 a month. Most owners start here.
- Full: $2,222 once. Adds proposals, deposit collection, and every customer channel the business uses. Optional care is $444 a month.
- Founding Grow: $750 for the first three owners, with a named testimonial required after the front desk has been running.

Care is optional. The front desk stays in the client's accounts if care ends. A later tier can be added to the existing build.

Soma is part of SynKasa. It carries one customer entry into the CRM, calendar, text thread, and working list.

The SynKasa fit form asks for contact details, business type, contact channels, weekly inquiry volume, current booking method, main problem, desired result, and implementation timing. A website or social page is optional.

## Siesie

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/siesie

Application: https://frimpomaasync.com/siesie-application

Siesie is the back office above the SynKasa ladder. It covers five roles:

1. Scheduling
2. Money
3. Coordination
4. Account management
5. Reporting

Siesie is $25,000 once. It is for an established business where four or five of those roles still return to the owner.

Before a Siesie build there is a paid diagnostic, the Operations Map: https://frimpomaasync.com/operations-map

The Operations Map is $2,500 and takes two weeks. It is credited in full against a Siesie build. It delivers six documents: the current-state map, the owner-dependency register, the cost of waiting, the future-state map, the sequenced and priced build plan, and a ninety-minute walkthrough. It costs the owner under four hours of their own time. If the map concludes a Siesie build is not right for the business, the fee is refunded and the owner keeps all six documents.

The representative path is: work received, scheduled, coordinated, invoiced, and reported.

The implementation path is: map, build, test, approve, launch, train, and hand over.

The owner supplies the current process, working rules, account access, and timely approvals. Judgment calls, exceptions, approvals, and sensitive conversations stay human.

The Siesie application asks for contact details, business type, team size, monthly job or client volume, current scheduling and invoicing processes, people being coordinated, owner-dependent work, the main bottleneck, implementation timing, and investment readiness. Website, current tools, and additional context are optional.

## Soft Appeals

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals

Sample audit report: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-audit

Patient data and privacy: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-your-data

Free denial decoder: https://frimpomaasync.com/soft-appeals-decoder · type any denial reason code (like CO-16, CO-29, CO-50, CO-197, PR-204) and get the plain-English meaning, whether it is a quick fix, an appeal or a dead claim, published win-rate context, the recommended move, and a sample appeal-letter opening. Runs entirely in the browser and asks for no patient information. Also carries a Maryland payer-by-payer appeal deadline table.

Soft Appeals recovers denied insurance claims for independent medical practices and outpatient groups. Maryland first. It is a separate audience from SynKasa and Siesie and does not serve local service businesses.

How it works: the practice signs a business associate agreement, sends its 20 most recent denials through a secure channel, and receives a free one-page audit within days. The audit sorts every claim into quick fixes, claims worth appealing, and claims not worth fighting, values each at the contracted allowed amount rather than billed charges, and flags claims whose appeal window closes soonest. AI drafts each appeal against the payer's own published rules, then NaNa Frimpomaa reads, corrects, signs and sends it with proof of delivery. The AI tools that touch claims operate under their own business associate agreements, and nothing trains on patient data. The practice approves every appeal before it is submitted in the practice's name.

Fee: 25 percent of commercial claims actually recovered, invoiced only after the payer pays the practice and matched to the payer's own remittance. Individual claims from $150, with smaller claims appealed in batches. Medicare and Medicaid claims carry a flat fee per appeal instead, because federal rules do not permit percentage fees on them. There is no setup fee, no monthly minimum, and no contract lock. No recovery means no fee.

The money goes from the payer directly to the practice. Soft Appeals never handles client funds.

Strong fit: therapy, physical and occupational therapy, dental, chiropractic, podiatry, and any independent practice writing off denials monthly. Wrong fit: hospitals and health systems. Substance use disorder claims are out of scope because of the federal rules covering those records.

Privacy commitments: a signed business associate agreement before any patient data moves, never ordinary email, never a consumer chatbot, work done inside the practice's own systems wherever possible, unique logins with two-factor sign-in, US-based with no offshoring, notification within 72 hours if anything goes wrong, and return or destruction of claim-level data when the engagement ends.

Soft Appeals makes no promise about recovery amounts or win rates. The published statistics on its pages are industry figures with named sources, not predictions about any practice.

## The method

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/method

Every engagement runs the same twelve steps: useful diagnosis, fit form, 15-minute call, recommendation, proposal and agreement, payment, onboarding, build and test, approval, launch and training, follow-up, and proof, referral, or care.

Inside the build there are seven phases, each producing a document the client keeps: map, build, test, approve, launch, train, and hand over. The seven documents are the Operations Map, the build shown as it stands up, the Test Record, written approvals, the Launch Log, the Operating Manual, and the Ownership Pack.

The testing standard is published in full on that page. Six checks must pass before launch: the normal path, the exception path, the failure path, the follow-up path, the data, and ownership. If a check cannot be ticked, the build does not launch and the date moves.

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/comparison

Siesie compared against hiring an operations person, buying software and configuring it yourself, and doing nothing. Salary figures are cited from ZipRecruiter, July 2026, and benefits from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, March 2026. The page also states when not to choose Siesie.

## About

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/about

frimpomaasync is one person, NaNa Frimpomaa. Background: hospital front desk and patient check-in, human resources, building hospital forms, performance improvement for a healthcare system, and SQL, data management and Epic go-lives. Weekday response inside four hours, a written update every Friday, two builds at a time, no subscription to frimpomaasync.

The page also lists what is not taken on: guaranteed bookings, websites, ads, ongoing content, answering customers on the owner's behalf, selling a larger build than needed, and automating a process nobody has written down.

## Your data during a build

Page: https://frimpomaasync.com/data

Covers a client engagement, not website visitors. Nothing is copied to a system frimpomaasync controls, and no database of the client's customers is held. Access is granted by the client to their own accounts, named in the scope, used only to configure, test and document, listed at handover, and revoked by the client. The page lists what each of the five Siesie roles touches and never touches. Card numbers, bank credentials and the client's money are never touched. Engagement records are kept for seven years; exports of client data are not retained. Anything held is deleted within 30 days on request. Unauthorised access is reported in writing within 72 hours.

## Privacy

Policy: https://frimpomaasync.com/privacy

Qualification forms collect only the business context a visitor chooses to submit. Public forms do not ask for passwords, payment details, customer records, private files, or account access.

Form submissions may include business type, inquiry or job volume, current process, desired result, timing, and investment readiness. They are used to review fit and prepare for the call.

Client systems are built in client-owned accounts. The signed agreement names every provider that handles client or customer data.

## Retired routes

The Client Catcher name is retired except for the "formerly" note. `/client-catcher`, `/services`, `/products`, `/solo-business-system`, and `/ai-products` redirect to `/synkasa`. `/soma` redirects to `/synkasa#soma`.
